title: Longitudinal modeling of the relationship between age and maximal heart rate
authors: Gellish RL, Goslin BR, Olson RE, McDonald A, Russi GD, Moudgil VK
population: Men and women of broad age and fitness range with repeated maximal graded exercise tests over 25 years at a university fitness centre
findings: Retrospective analysis of 908 maximal graded exercise tests from 132 individuals tested repeatedly between 1978 and 2003.
Linear mixed-models gave HRmax = 207 - 0.7 x age (P < 0.001).
The longitudinal equation is appreciably different from 220 - age and confirms recent cross-sectional findings.
limitations: Single-centre retrospective fitness-centre sample; N = 132 individuals; not runner-specific; abstract reports no individual-level error. The abstract does not explicitly state that the within-person slope equals the cross-sectional slope; it says the result confirms cross-sectional investigations.
implications: A within-person HRmax decline of about 0.7 bpm per year of age is supported longitudinally (inference from the equation slope): when only an older measured HRmax exists, age-adjust it by about 0.7 bpm per year elapsed, with low confidence.
Gellish (207) and Tanaka (208) are practically identical; implement one equation, not both.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (title case differs only). Europe PMC abstract confirms N=132, 908 tests, 207 - 0.7 x age. Researcher's claim that the within-person slope 'matched the cross-sectional slope' was reworded to the abstract's 'confirms cross-sectional findings'.
